name: Anti-Signal Recognition Particle Necrotizing Myopathy
aliases: Immune-Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy with Anti-SRP Antibodies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: European Neuromuscular Centre (ENMC) 2016 Criteria for Immune-Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy

criteria.description: Presence of anti-SRP autoantibodies in serum
Muscle biopsy showing necrotizing myopathy with minimal inflammatory infiltrate
Symmetric proximal muscle weakness clinically evident
Markedly elevated serum creatine kinase levels

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of anti-SRP antibodies plus muscle biopsy showing necrotizing myopathy with compatible clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other inflammatory myopathies and muscular dystrophies.

laboratory: Elevated serum creatine kinase (CK) often >10x normal
imaging: Muscle MRI showing muscle edema and fatty replacement
Chest imaging to evaluate for interstitial lung disease if suspected
other: Muscle biopsy demonstrating necrotic muscle fibers with minimal inflammatory infiltrate
Electromyography showing myopathic motor unit potentials

distinguishingFeatures: More prominent inflammatory infiltrates on biopsy

redFlags: Rapidly progressive muscle weakness leading to respiratory failure
Markedly elevated CK with acute onset
Cardiac arrhythmias or cardiomyopathy in a patient with muscle weakness
references: Allenbach Y, et al. Immune-mediated necrotizing myopathies: clinical features and pathogenesis. Nat Rev Rheumatol. 2020.
European Neuromuscular Centre (ENMC) 2016 International Workshop: Classification of Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathies.
Lundberg IE, et al. 2017 EULAR/ACR Classification Criteria for Adult and Juvenile Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathies and Their Major Subgroups. Arthritis Rheumatol.
